headline: BTC $83.6k at range lows into Bitget's 04:00 UTC withdrawal deadline; SOL +3.4%
summary: At 21:19 UTC on 25 September BTC is $83,619.70 against an $84,380.00 open (-0.90%), sitting only 22% up its $83,163.60-$85,247.40 band, ETH is $2,677.12 (-0.38%) and the weakest of the three at 13% of its $2,667.23-$2,742.42 range, while SOL is $121.05 (+3.44%), 74% up its range and still the week's leader at +7.1% against +3.4% for BTC and +2.0% for ETH. The drift lower is macro, not crypto: the US 10-year Treasury yield eased about 5bp to 5.16% after touching a 19-year high on Wednesday-Thursday, odds of a 25bp October Fed hike slipped to roughly 66% from 72% within 24 hours, and Japan's 10-year pushed toward 3.1%, its highest since 1996 - the bond complex, not spot selling, set this week's lows. The one acute story is still open: Bitget's breach estimate stands at $387.5m after Zcash and TRON transfers were added to the $351.6m first reported, withdrawals remain suspended while deposits and trading run, and the exchange has only promised to publish a resumption plan by 04:00 UTC on 26 September - hours away, into a weekend. Positioning keeps getting lighter rather than heavier, which is the setup in which dips have historically been shallow: Hyperliquid BTC open interest is down to $3.19bn from $3.29bn, BTC funding has collapsed to 0.00018%/h from 0.00125%/h, and the BTC futures premium is -0.063% with SOL at -0.006%, so spot is trading above futures. Fear & Greed is 71 and the composite reads 60.6, both Greed, on 243 items in 24 hours - a de-levered, range-bound tape pinned at the low end by real yields, with one custody question due to resolve overnight.

BTC.note: $83,619.70, down 0.90% and 1.9% off the $85,247.40 high, pinned at 22% of an $83,163.60-$85,247.40 band with open interest down to $3.19bn and the futures premium at -0.063%, deeper below spot than the -0.022% four hours ago - the marginal seller is leverage leaving, not spot distribution, and this is drift within the range rather than a dip.

ETH.note: $2,677.12, down 0.38% and the weakest of the three at 13% of a $2,667.23-$2,742.42 range after failing at $2,742; the premium has ticked back to +0.007% from -0.011% with open interest flat at $2.96bn and funding at 0.00125%/h, so there is neither a crowded long nor a bid here.

SOL.note: $121.05, up 3.44% and 74% up its $115.85-$122.91 range, +7.1% on the week and part of a broad large-alt rotation, on the thinnest book of the three at $742m of open interest - most reflexive in both directions, and it carries the 28 September Alpenglow activation two days out.

drivers.title: Bitget still frozen at $387.5m: resumption plan due 04:00 UTC 26 September
drivers.detail: Bitget's loss estimate stands at $387.5m, revised up from the $351.6m first confirmed on 24 September after the investigation added affected Zcash and TRON transfers; CEO Gracy Chen says private keys were not compromised - attackers breached a wallet backend and spoofed transfer data so Bitget's own authorization process approved the payouts - and cites IP and on-chain patterns matching North Korean state-linked activity. Withdrawals remain suspended pending a security review while deposits and trading continue, Circle and Tether have frozen attacker wallets, and a 5% recovery bounty is live for anyone who helps freeze or recover funds. The exchange has committed only to publishing a resumption plan by 1 p.m. KST on 26 September, which is 04:00 UTC, after that timetable already slipped once - the deadline lands overnight into thin weekend books.

drivers.title: Real yields remain the price-setter: 10-year 5.16% off a 19-year high, October hike odds 66%
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield eased roughly 5bp to 5.16% on Friday after a two-session surge to its highest level since 2007, the move that pulled BTC from about $87,265 on Wednesday to under $84,000 on Thursday. The cause has not gone away: the preliminary September S&P Global composite PMI printed 58.4, the fastest US business expansion since 2021, which pushed market-implied odds of a 25bp Fed hike in October to about 70% before drifting back to 66% from 72% over the last 24 hours, with 50bp odds at nil. Bond volatility is elevated while bitcoin and equities stay calm, so a resumption of the yield rise is the single most likely cause of a break of $83,163.

drivers.title: Iran names its price for reopening Hormuz in seven days
drivers.detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, in a private gathering on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on 24 September, set out a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within seven days if Washington lifts its naval blockade, waives sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observes a ceasefire extending to Lebanon; US and Iranian negotiators are separately exploring a phased version with Qatari mediation. Markets priced relief immediately - WTI fell about 3% to $91.74, Brent about 1% to roughly $105, gold rose nearly 1% above $4,300 and the dollar index slipped below 101 - but the conditions attached are large, and a June 17 memorandum on the same trade already collapsed into renewed fighting. This is the biggest single source of potential relief for yields and therefore for crypto, and also the biggest single source of reversal risk.

drivers.title: Leverage keeps draining: BTC funding near zero, premium at -0.063%
drivers.detail: Hyperliquid BTC open interest has fallen again to $3.19bn from $3.29bn four hours earlier and $4.02bn on 22 September, ETH is flat at $2.96bn and SOL is $742m. The clearer signal is in the cost of carry: BTC funding has collapsed to 0.00018%/h from a flat 0.00125%/h, the BTC futures premium has gone further negative to -0.063% and SOL sits at -0.006%, so spot trades above futures on two of the three. That follows Friday's 08:00 UTC expiry of roughly $15.6bn of Deribit options, the largest of the year, which cleared without a break, and a 24 September hour in which about $237m of longs were liquidated. Crowding is 59.8 on the composite and the ai_calm component is the weakest at 40.0 - a tape with the leverage already flushed out, which is historically the condition in which dips have been shallow rather than structural.

drivers.title: Trump-Xi state visit ends with a truce extension to 10 January and little else
drivers.detail: The White House confirmed at 20:10 UTC that the three-day Xi state visit had concluded; the deliverable is an extension of the expiring US-China trade truce to 10 January, a two-month rollover of the Busan agreement that lowered US tariffs and suspended Beijing's rare-earth and critical-mineral export controls. There were no purchase commitments, no AI-risk agreement and no movement on Iran. For crypto this removes a near-term tariff shock but only for two months, and it puts a hard date on the calendar rather than settling anything.

drivers.title: Regulated money still adding while Washington stalls and money rotates into alts
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs ran six consecutive inflow sessions worth about $2.8bn through Thursday - $999m Monday, $714.75m Tuesday, $347m Wednesday, $191m Thursday with IBIT at roughly $163m of that and about $1.35bn across the streak - flipping 2026 year-to-date net flows positive to about $787m. The pace decayed 81% from Monday's peak, so the bid is fading at the margin, but regulated money kept adding on the exact sessions when the 10-year hit 19-year highs. Inside crypto the bid has rotated to large alts rather than out: 93 of the 100 CoinDesk 100 constituents rose, with QNT +38%, ONDO +28% and LINK +11%. On the corporate side Strategy filed an 8-K at 15:23 UTC seeking shareholder approval to accrue preferred dividends 365 days a year to pull STRC back toward $100, while the legislative channel stays shut after the CLARITY Act's 49-50 cloture failure on 15 September pushed market-structure work to the regulators.

watch.what: Bitget's committed deadline to publish a withdrawal resumption plan (1 p.m. KST). This timetable already slipped once and the loss estimate rose 10% with it. A clean reopening closes the only acute crypto story on the board; a second delay, over a weekend with thin books, is the item most capable of turning a covered exchange loss into a broader confidence event about exchange balances.

US-Iran technical talks on a phased Hormuz reopening, against Tehran's seven-day proposal conditioned on lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and a ceasefire including Lebanon. Progress is the cleanest path to lower oil and lower yields; a collapse puts the 10-year back at 19-year highs and BTC back under $83,163.

Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation (Agave 4.3), the largest protocol change of the quarter, landing on the thinnest book of the three at $742m of open interest and after a +7.1% week - SOL carries the most positioning risk into it.

BEA Personal Income and Outlays with the August PCE deflator (08:30 ET), plus ADP at 12:15 UTC and Consumer Confidence at 14:00 UTC, all on quarter-end when flows get pulled around. With October hike odds at 66% after a 58.4 flash PMI, a hot core print prices the hike close to certain and is the most direct scheduled risk to dip-buying.
September Employment Situation (nonfarm payrolls, 08:30 ET). First-Friday payrolls into a Fed that markets already expect to hike in October; September CPI follows on 14 October.
Expiry of the extended US-China trade truce agreed during this week's state visit. Not a near-term risk, but it is the new hard date on the tariff calendar and no broader deal was struck.

Context for any pullback, from the stored history only: BTC has had 28 sharp dips, with +1.5% recovered within 14 days in 92.9% of cases (median 5.0 h, 78.6% within 24 h) and a typical extra drop after the trigger of -0.5%; ETH 91 dips at 92.3% (median 5.0 h) and SOL 132 dips at 93.9% (median 3.5 h, typical extra drop -0.3%). Dips during greed recovered 7 of 7 for BTC, 92.9% of 28 for ETH and 93.8% of 48 for SOL. Today's market state most resembles 2025-07-11, 2025-10-04 and 2024-07-21, after which BTC's median 30-day move was 8.0% (up in 60.0% of them). The one precursor to respect: 'Donald Trump (Truth Social) + inflation/CPI' preceded a BTC dip within 6h 2.6% of the time versus 1.0% by chance (2.72x lift, n=115, held in both halves of the data).
